subject: french

moments.title: Loi Deixonne
moments.body: After decades of repression, regional languages (Breton, Basque, Catalan, Occitan) are allowed to be taught in schools.
moments.takeaway: France's diversity was long denied institutionally.

moments.title: Constitution amendment
moments.body: Article 2 declares French 'the language of the Republic', complicating regional language protection.

moments.title: Regional languages constitutional
moments.body: Article 75-1 recognises regional languages as part of France's heritage.
moments.takeaway: Recognition does not necessarily mean support.

now.title: Regional languages today
now.body: Bilingual schools (Diwan in Brittany, calandretes in Occitania) operate with mixed legal status. The Falloux law on minority-language teachers continues to provoke debate.
now.open_questions: Will France's minority languages survive as living tongues?

reflection: France's linguistic uniformity was achieved at the cost of many other tongues.
